summary: Phase 136M, independent verification. Independently re-derived and adversarially attacked Phase 136L's Group 3 executable schemas (CutoverRequest, ReadinessPackage) from primary sources (CLTR-CUTOVER-EXECUTABLE-SCHEMAS-001 v1.0 Sec.7/9/10/12/19/19.1(136D-repaired)/20/46, plus the 136E implementation plan's own Group 3 section), not from 136L's own tests, prose, or findings. Cross-checked Sec.46's original per-file grouping (cutover_request alone as Group 3, readiness_package alone as a separate Group 4) against the 136E implementation plan's coarser, explicitly reasoned re-grouping of both files under one Group 3 label, and confirmed this is a disclosed, non-contradictory renumbering, not a silent mismatch. Independently re-derived and re-attacked the $ref dependency graph and the record-identity/digest dependency graph, confirming no cycle and no versioned request-v2 mechanism exists in actual schema behavior. Re-attacked Tier 1 strictness (target/source_authority/authorization_requirement constants), the 10-value request state machine, source/target authority epoch bindings, evidence-family separation (readiness_package_reference restricted to exactly readiness_package; evidence_references independently re-tested against all 16 record_family values), the authorization-requirement boundary (no embedded authorization proof), identity/digest honesty, Tier 2's _extensions boundary (string-valued map only, no critical smuggling), the exact readiness-category/result vocabularies (state, prerequisite_status, gate_result, findings[].verdict), and the conflict/BLOCKING-finding invariant -- including two new attack vectors 136L's suite did not exercise (a ready state carrying an open BLOCKING finding, confirmed a Layer 4 responsibility per Sec.40, not a Layer 2 defect; and duplicate finding IDs/evidence references, confirmed unenforced by Sec.20's own text). Disclosed four new NON-BLOCKING/DEFERRED findings, none repaired within Group 3's bounded scope: (1) shared/identity.schema.json's generic record_id pattern does not enforce Sec.10's documented per-family prefix convention -- no security impact, since record_type/record_family remain the actual, correctly-enforced family tags, and fixing this would require changing a Group-1 shared definition consumed by all four production record schemas, outside this phase's Group-3-bounded repair scope; (2) the manifest's declared dependencies array is not cross-checked against the actual $ref graph (informational metadata only; true cycle-freedom is independently proven via the $ref/identity graph tests, not manifest metadata); (3) an in-range-but-semantically-wrong implementation_group value is not locally detected by manifest verification (authoring-review responsibility; both Group 3 entries independently re-confirmed correct as currently authored); (4) ReadinessPackage's ready/BLOCKING-finding combination, and duplicate finding IDs/evidence references, are not locally rejected (matches this contract's existing, disclosed shape-only philosophy; Layer 4's cross-field consistency responsibility per Sec.40). Zero BLOCKING findings. Added 98 new independent tests (tests/test_cltr_cutover_136m_request_and_readiness_independent_verification.py). Combined test_cltr_cutover_136h/i/j/k/l/m + test_schema_runtime_* suite: 932 passed, 0 failed (834 baseline + 98 new). Fast Green: 4391 passed, identical to the 136H/136I/136J/136K/136L baseline, zero regressions. Full unmarked suite freshly run on a quiescent working tree: 20991 passed, 19 failed, 21010 total, 1261.41s -- all 19 failing node IDs byte-identical file-for-file to the established inherited-failure baseline (test_advisory_runtime_contract.py, test_advisory_runtime_architecture.py, test_phase_reports.py, test_rendering_134e5.py, test_finalization_transaction_134e10.py x5, test_cltr_migration_135p_verification.py x4, test_bootstrap_todo_consistency.py x2, test_cltr_135o_integration.py x4), zero new failures -- the single transient concurrency-caused extra failure 136L disclosed as NON-BLOCKING-136L-4 (test_commit_push_preflight.py::test_no_repo_mutation) did not recur, since this run had no concurrent task-lifecycle writes, satisfying 136L's own stated next-verification requirement. Legacy lifecycle remains the sole production authority; CLTR remains derivative; runtime remains Observed / observe / execution unavailable. No HumanAuthorization, CutoverCandidate, Certification, or any later-group record schema, typed model, semantic validator, or authority resolver/state/pointer was created or changed. Verdict: VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- READY FOR AUTHORIZATION AND CANDIDATE SCHEMA IMPLEMENTATION. Recommended next phase: 136N -- Authorization and Candidate Schema Implementation.

validation_results.result: Independently re-confirmed exactly four production record schemas, exactly 11 manifest entries, and cross-checked Sec.46's original per-file grouping (cutover_request Group 3 alone, readiness_package Group 4 alone) against the 136E implementation plan's coarser, explicitly reasoned re-grouping -- confirmed a disclosed, non-contradictory renumbering.

validation_results.result: Independently rebuilt the $ref dependency graph (textual scan: neither Group 3 file $refs the other) and the record-identity/digest dependency graph (both use the same generic, family-agnostic shared $defs) -- no cycle, no request-v2 mechanism, confirming BLOCKING-136D-1's repair is reflected in actual schema behavior.

validation_results.name: tier1_strictness_reattack
validation_results.result: Fresh fixtures: target=legacy, source_authority=cltr, authorization_requirement=false/null, case/whitespace variants of target, and _extensions on cutover_request all rejected.

validation_results.name: evidence_family_separation_all_16_families
validation_results.result: readiness_package_reference independently re-attacked with 4 wrong families, all rejected; evidence_references independently re-tested against all 16 record_family enum values, all accepted, matching Sec.20's no-restriction text; an unknown family rejected.

validation_results.name: conflict_blocking_invariant_and_new_attack_vectors
validation_results.result: conflict without a BLOCKING finding, and conflict with only a NON-BLOCKING finding, both rejected. New vectors: a ready state carrying an open BLOCKING finding, and duplicate finding IDs/evidence references, are all accepted -- independently confirmed as genuine Layer 4 (Sec.40) responsibilities, not Layer 2 defects.

validation_results.name: manifest_tamper_reattack
validation_results.result: Out-of-range implementation_group (99) and missing Group 3 entry both correctly rejected. Two new disclosed limitations: an injected spurious dependency edge, and an in-range-but-wrong implementation_group value, both load successfully -- disclosed as authoring-review-level metadata gaps, not schema-security defects.

validation_results.name: record_id_cross_family_prefix_finding
validation_results.result: New independent finding: record_id's shared generic pattern does not enforce Sec.10's per-family prefix convention, but record_type/record_family remain the actual, correctly enforced security-relevant tags. Disclosed as NON-BLOCKING-136M-1, DEFERRED, out of Group-3-bounded repair scope.
